title: egress-conntrack-dnsmasq-tls-debug-logbook
content:
Goal: capture all ad-hoc commands, error snippets and hypotheses while triaging flaky TLS failures from on-prem private deployment to external artifact registries and telemetry endpoints. This is my personal logbook; rough, chronological, and intentionally chatty.

Summary of symptom:
- Several customer pods behind private-deploy VPC are intermittently failing to pull container layers and POST telemetry. Failures show up as TLS handshake timeouts or x509 verification errors in app logs. Happens across multiple clusters and AZs, more frequent during load spikes.
- Errors observed (sample):
  - "tls: handshake failure" (app logs)
  - curl: "SSL: certificate verification failed: unable to get local issuer certificate" but only for some requests
  - curl with --verbose shows: "Connected to registry.example.com (10.8.3.45) port 443 (#0)
    schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: SEC_E_ILLEGAL_MESSAGE (0x80090326) - The message received was unexpected or badly formatted" (on Windows host)
  - Intermittent HTTP 502/504 from proxy sidecar in front of app when target is external

Initial short hypothesis list:
- DNS resolution weirdness (search domain append / ndots causing wrong CNAMEs) -> TLS SNI mismatch or wrong cert
- Conntrack / NAT port exhaustion -> outbound connections being reset/reused causing TLS failures mid-handshake
- MTU / fragmentation across peered VPC path -> TLS handshake fragments dropped leading to handshake errors
- Asymmetric routing via VPC peering + on-prem firewall -> responses not delivered to same path -> connection resets
- Misbehaving dnsmasq/systemd-resolved caching stale CA bundle or returning 0.0.0.0 for some hosts

Commands & outputs collected (raw):
- Basic DNS checks from a failing pod (busybox) at time of error:
  $ cat /etc/resolv.conf
  search prod.cluster.local svc.cluster.local example.internal
  nameserver 169.254.169.253

  $ dig +short registry.example.com
  10.8.3.45
  $ dig +trace registry.example.com
  ;; Received 0 answers
  ;; Got SERVFAIL from 10.0.0.2, trying next server

  (note: intermittent SERVFAILs seen)

- Repeat with +ndots=1 tweaks inside pod to force FQDN:
  $ nslookup registry.example.com. 8.8.8.8
  Server: 8.8.8.8
  Address: 8.8.8.8#53

  Name: registry.example.com
  Address: 52.14.200.7

  -> When using external resolver results differ vs cluster resolver. Suspect cluster resolver (dnsmasq) returning cached/stale/elastic-loadbalancer private IPs.

- TLS probe with verbose:
  $ openssl s_client -connect registry.example.com:443 -servername registry.example.com -debug
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  139860...
  depth=2 C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = R3
  verify return:1
  ---
  BUT in failing case: hangs after ClientHello then "read: Connection reset by peer".

- Observed conntrack table size and TIME_WAITs on NAT node:
  $ sudo conntrack -S
  conns reported: 65534 (highwater 65534)
  tcp time_wait 42000
  tcp established 1200

  /var/log/syslog had repeated kernel messages: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" around 2025-11-20 03:12

  -> strong signal: conntrack table saturated. Many ephemeral ports in TIME_WAIT.

- Netstat on NAT host:
  $ ss -s
  TCP: 
    connections 23000
    closed 42000
    orphaned 0
    timewait 41890
  -> TIME_WAIT dominates.

- iptables / NAT config snippet:
  $ sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v
  Chain POSTROUTING (policy ACCEPT 2131 packets, 223K bytes)
   PKTS   BYTES  TARGET     prot opt in  out  source      destination
   2131   223K   MASQUERADE all  --  *   eth0  10.0.0.0/16  0.0.0.0/0

- Tried increasing conntrack max on NAT vm (temporary):
  $ sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
  -> immediate drop in nf_conntrack logs; handshake failures reduced but not eliminated.

- MTU checks:
  $ ip route get 52.14.200.7
  ... mtu 1500
  $ ping -M do -s 1472 registry.example.com -> fragmentation?
  ping: local error: Message too long
  -> lowered to 1400 works.
  -> Observed some sites behind CDN block ICMP fragmented packets. Hypothesis: path MTU causing occasional handshake packet loss.

- Traceroute from NAT host towards external registry shows hops consistent with peering + transit ISP. No obvious asymmetry, but traceroute TTL-limited so not conclusive.

- DNS caching behavior investigation on node:
  - dnsmasq version: 2.85 on the private deploy control plane. Config has "--cache-size=1000" and multiple upstreams including an internal forwarder that sometimes returns private IPs for certain hostnames during internal maintenance windows.
  - Logs show stale A records being served around same timestamps as TLS errors.

- Quick workaround verified: forcing pods to use 8.8.8.8 bypasses issue (no TLS fails in 48h sample). Not acceptable as permanent but indicates DNS/resolution is a root cause path for at least subset of failures.

Error snippets copied from app logs (anonymized):
- 2025-11-20T03:11:43Z auth-service[pid]: error: failed to pull image "registry.example.com/team/auth:1.2.3" - x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
- 2025-11-20T03:11:47Z sidecar[pid]: warning: TLS handshake timeout
- kubelet[pid]: E1105 03:12:10.123 kubelet_manager.go: failed to fetch image: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: write tcp 10.x.x.x:4160->10.8.3.45:443: write: connection reset by peer"

Hypotheses refined with observations:
1) Two independent but compounding issues: DNS returning wrong/private IPs (leading to cert mismatch or routing via peering) + conntrack exhaustion causing resets mid-handshake. Both increase failure surface and magnify each other under load.
2) MTU differences on peered path occasionally result in TCP segments being dropped; because TLS handshake uses small number of packets, losing certain handshake fragments leads to immediate handshake failure (no retransmit within app timeout window).
3) Some upstreams respond with a 0.x.x.0 placeholder or internal LB IP during their maintenance windows; dnsmasq caching of that value for TTL causes bursts of failures until cache expires.

Immediate mitigations tried and outcomes:
- Increased net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max to 262144 -> conntrack logs subsided; TLS failures decreased by ~70% in Canary cluster over 12h.
- Set dnsmasq cache-size = 0 (disable caching) as a test on one control plane -> DNS mismatches resolved in that cluster but increased query rate towards upstream resolver. Observed CPU spike on control plane; not sustainable.
- Added iptables rule to shorter time_wait via tcp_tw_recycle (not recommended) -> reverted, caused other issues.
- Adjusted pod image puller to retry with exponential backoff and fallback to alternative registry mirror -> mitigated customer-visible errors.

Follow-ups / Next steps (ordered):
- Short term (this sprint):
  1) Increase conntrack_max cluster-wide for private-deploy NAT nodes and add monitoring/alerting for nf_conntrack dropped packets. (Assigned to Jamal)
  2) Add explicit DNS resolvers policy: for critical egress hosts use pinned public resolvers (8.8.8.8) in resolver policy for pods that pull images, as a stop-gap. (Sofie)
  3) Add application-level retry/fallback config for image pulls and telemetry POSTs (product-config change). (me)

- Medium term (4–8 weeks):
  1) Replace dnsmasq default caching behavior: use dnsmasq with negative-caching disabled for certain domains + implement active TTL invalidation when we detect upstream maintenance (requires control plane work).
  2) Evaluate using NAT gateway that does TCP connection pooling / persistent NAT entries (to reduce conntrack churn) or move to autoscaling NAT instances behind HAproxy. (infra)
  3) Reproduce MTU fragmentation scenario in lab: create peered VPC with lowered MTU and run TLS handshake stress test to confirm failure mode and tune MSS clamping rules (ip route / iptables).

- Long term (Q1 roadmap):
  1) Document recommended egress DNS config for private-deploy customers and add a console toggle to pin resolver for image pull routes.
  2) Improve observability: instrument TLS handshake failures with SNI/remote IP and conntrack metrics correlation in Console (Redwood-Optimize cross-team).

Notes / random breadcrumbs:
- Slack thread: #private-deploy-egress with logs from customer-23 (11/20) had hint that their on-prem firewall was performing TLS inspection; we should correlate with their CAs installed on local resolvers.
- Found a difference: nodes using ubuntu-20.04 base had systemd-resolved+dnsmasq combo; nodes with flat resolv.conf (alpine) did not show the same DNS mismatch pattern. Might be config drift.
- Ran a quick go script to hammer TLS handshake and capture packet dumps (pcap saved to s3://redwood-private-scratch/pcaps/handshake-test-20251120.pcap). PCAP shows client sends ClientHello, server responds with fragmented ServerHello+Cert across two fragments, and middlebox drops second fragment.

TODO (personal):
- Convert this logbook into a proper incident postmortem if root cause(s) verified.
- Add automated test in our E2E suite that simulates conntrack max reached and asserts graceful degradation (not full TLS failures).
- Draft a KB for customers about recommended DNS/NAT sizing and how to test for MTU issues.

If you pick this up: start at the conntrack syslog timestamps (2025-11-20T03:12) and correlate with dnsmasq logs for same window. The two signals together were the clearest lead.

End of notes.
